tell: A nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, with about 80% of the dose excreted in urine.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is 44%, and a high-fat meal does not meaningfully change exposure. It is 92% bound to plasma protein, mainly albumin, and mostly metabolized by CYP3A4.
A crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water, with a molecular weight of 378.43 g/mol.
Approved under an NDA as 10, 20 and 40 mg film-coated tablets, dosed once daily.
No boxed warning; contraindicated with adrenal insufficiency and with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Hyperkalemia and hypotension are the most frequent adverse reactions.
Reducing kidney and cardiovascular risk in adults with chronic kidney disease associated with type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular risk in adults with heart failure and LVEF of 40% or more.
A nonsteroidal, selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist with no relevant affinity for androgen, progesterone, estrogen or glucocorticoid receptors.
The generic name begins with F and has ten letters.
